correctness.rationale: The exact theorem and proof were read in the open arXiv full text and the relevant pages were visually inspected. Scaling the universally quantified test vector g by t makes every integral term linear in t while leaving gamma||K*f||^2 fixed; division and t->infinity therefore rigorously removes gamma. The two resulting energy inequalities give the stated bounds, and one-point scalar examples attain both factors exactly.

value.rationale: Theorem 4.1 presents gamma as a K-directed perturbation allowance and uses it both in the admissibility threshold and in the frame bounds. Under the printed quantifiers gamma has no mathematical effect at all. Removing the spurious restriction and identifying the two best universal constants materially changes the stability theorem rather than merely simplifying notation.
